The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe. With their great intellect and flying skills, these Pokémon very successfully act as the Galar region’s airborne taxi service.

title: Blipbug
text: Blipbug, the Larva Pokémon (Bug type). A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn’t. Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.

title: Dottler
text: Dottler, the Radome Pokémon (Bug/Psychic type). It barely moves, but it’s still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers. As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.

title: Orbeetle
text: Orbeetle, the Seven Spot Pokémon (Bug/Psychic type). It’s famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power. It emits psychic energy to observe and study what’s around it—and what’s around it can include things over six miles away.

title: Nickit
text: Nickit, the Fox Pokémon (Dark type). Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains. Cunning and cautious, this Pokémon survives by stealing food from others. It erases its tracks with swipes of its tail as it makes off with its plunder.

title: Thievul
text: Thievul, the Fox Pokémon (Dark type). It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it. With a lithe body and sharp claws, it goes around stealing food and eggs. Boltund is its natural enemy.

title: Gossifleur
text: Gossifleur, the Flowering Pokémon (Grass type). It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly. It whirls around in the wind while singing a joyous song. This delightful display has charmed many into raising this Pokémon.

title: Eldegoss
text: Eldegoss, the Cotton Bloom Pokémon (Grass type). The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them. The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.

title: Wooloo
text: Wooloo, the Sheep Pokémon (Normal type). Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed. If its fleece grows too long, Wooloo won’t be able to move. Cloth made with the wool of this Pokémon is surprisingly strong.

title: Dubwool
text: Dubwool, the Sheep Pokémon (Normal type). Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You’ll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it. Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.

title: Chewtle
text: Chewtle, the Snapping Pokémon (Water type). Apparently the itch of its teething impels it to snap its jaws at anything in front of it. It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.

title: Drednaw
text: Drednaw, the Bite Pokémon (Water/Rock type). With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey. This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.

title: Yamper
text: Yamper, the Puppy Pokémon (Electric type). This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail. This gluttonous Pokémon only assists people with their work because it wants treats. As it runs, it crackles with electricity.

title: Boltund
text: Boltund, the Dog Pokémon (Electric type). This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days. It sends electricity through its legs to boost their strength. Running at top speed, it easily breaks 50 mph.

title: Rolycoly
text: Rolycoly, the Coal Pokémon (Rock type). Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago. It can race around like a unicycle, even on rough, rocky terrain. Burning coal sustains it.

title: Carkol
text: Carkol, the Coal Pokémon (Rock/Fire type). It forms coal inside its body. Coal dropped by this Pokémon once helped fuel the lives of people in the Galar region. By rapidly rolling its legs, it can travel at over 18 mph. The temperature of the flames it breathes exceeds 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit.

title: Coalossal
text: Coalossal, the Coal Pokémon (Rock/Fire type). It’s usually peaceful, but the vandalism of mines enrages it. Offenders will be incinerated with flames that reach 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit. While it’s engaged in battle, its mountain of coal will burn bright red, sending off sparks that scorch the surrounding area.

title: Applin
text: Applin, the Apple Core Pokémon (Grass/Dragon type). It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it’s just an apple and nothing more. As soon as it’s born, it burrows into an apple. Not only does the apple serve as its food source, but the flavor of the fruit determines its evolution.

title: Flapple
text: Flapple, the Apple Wing Pokémon (Grass/Dragon type). It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns. It flies on wings of apple skin and spits a powerful acid. It can also change its shape into that of an apple.

title: Appletun
text: Appletun, the Apple Nectar Pokémon (Grass/Dragon type). Eating a sweet apple caused its evolution. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on. Its body is covered in sweet nectar, and the skin on its back is especially yummy. Children used to have it as a snack.

title: Silicobra
text: Silicobra, the Sand Snake Pokémon (Ground type). As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand. It spews sand from its nostrils. While the enemy is blinded, it burrows into the ground to hide.

title: Sandaconda
text: Sandaconda, the Sand Snake Pokémon (Ground type). When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened. Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.

title: Cramorant
text: Cramorant, the Gulp Pokémon (Flying/Water type). It’s so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it’s battling midfight. This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.

title: Arrokuda
text: Arrokuda, the Rush Pokémon (Water type). If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It’s very proud of that jaw. After it’s eaten its fill, its movements become extremely sluggish. That’s when Cramorant swallows it up.

title: Barraskewda
text: Barraskewda, the Skewer Pokémon (Water type). This Pokémon has a jaw that’s as sharp as a spear and as strong as steel. Apparently Barraskewda’s flesh is surprisingly tasty, too. It spins its tail fins to propel itself, surging forward at speeds of over 100 knots before ramming prey and spearing into them.

title: Toxel
text: Toxel, the Baby Pokémon (Electric/Poison type). It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows. It manipulates the chemical makeup of its poison to produce electricity. The voltage is weak, but it can cause a tingling paralysis.

title: Toxtricity
text: Toxtricity, the Punk Pokémon (Electric/Poison type). Other forms: Low Key Toxtricity (Electric/Poison). When this Pokémon sounds as if it’s strumming a guitar, it’s actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity. This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.

title: Sizzlipede
text: Sizzlipede, the Radiator Pokémon (Fire/Bug type). It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot. It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they’re well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.

title: Centiskorch
text: Centiskorch, the Radiator Pokémon (Fire/Bug type). When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies. While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.

title: Clobbopus
text: Clobbopus, the Tantrum Pokémon (Fighting type). It’s very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land. Its tentacles tear off easily, but it isn’t alarmed when that happens—it knows they’ll grow back. It’s about as smart as a three-year-old.

title: Grapploct
text: Grapploct, the Jujitsu Pokémon (Fighting type). A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful. Searching for an opponent to test its skills against, it emerges onto land. Once the battle is over, it returns to the sea.

title: Sinistea
text: Sinistea, the Black Tea Pokémon (Ghost type). This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea. The teacup in which this Pokémon makes its home is a famous piece of antique tableware. Many forgeries are in circulation.

title: Polteageist
text: Polteageist, the Black Tea Pokémon (Ghost type). This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found. Leaving leftover black tea unattended is asking for this Pokémon to come along and pour itself into it, turning the tea into a new Polteageist.

title: Hatenna
text: Hatenna, the Calm Pokémon (Psychic type). Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures’ emotions. If you don’t have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you. If this Pokémon senses a strong emotion, it will run away as fast as it can. It prefers areas without people.

title: Hattrem
text: Hattrem, the Serene Pokémon (Psychic type). No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently. Using the braids on its head, it pummels foes to get them to quiet down. One blow from those braids would knock out a professional boxer.

title: Hatterene
text: Hatterene, the Silent Pokémon (Psychic/Fairy type). It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others. If you’re too loud around it, you risk being torn apart by the claws on its tentacle. This Pokémon is also known as the Forest Witch.

title: Impidimp
text: Impidimp, the Wily Pokémon (Dark/Fairy type). Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy. It sneaks into people’s homes, stealing things and feasting on the negative energy of the frustrated occupants.

title: Morgrem
text: Morgrem, the Devious Pokémon (Dark/Fairy type). When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it’s trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair. With sly cunning, it tries to lure people into the woods. Some believe it to have the power to make crops grow.

title: Grimmsnarl
text: Grimmsnarl, the Bulk Up Pokémon (Dark/Fairy type). With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp. Its hairs work like muscle fibers. When its hairs unfurl, they latch on to opponents, ensnaring them as tentacles would.

title: Obstagoon
text: Obstagoon, the Blocking Pokémon (Dark/Normal type). Its voice is staggering in volume. Obstagoon has a tendency to take on a threatening posture and shout—this move is known as Obstruct. It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

title: Perrserker
text: Perrserker, the Viking Pokémon (Steel type). What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle. After many battles, it evolved dangerous claws that come together to form daggers when extended.

title: Cursola
text: Cursola, the Coral Pokémon (Ghost type). Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon’s core spirit. Be cautious of the ectoplasmic body surrounding its soul. You’ll become stiff as stone if you touch it.

title: Sirfetch’d
text: Sirfetch’d, the Wild Duck Pokémon (Fighting type). Only Farfetch’d that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon’s leek withers, it will retire from combat. After deflecting attacks with its hard leaf shield, it strikes back with its sharp leek stalk. The leek stalk is both weapon and food.

title: Mr. Rime
text: Mr. Rime, the Comedian Pokémon (Ice/Psychic type). It’s highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements. Its amusing movements make it very popular. It releases its psychic power from the pattern on its belly.

title: Runerigus
text: Runerigus, the Grudge Pokémon (Ground/Ghost type). A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move. Never touch its shadowlike body, or you’ll be shown the horrific memories behind the picture carved into it.

title: Milcery
text: Milcery, the Cream Pokémon (Fairy type). This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream. They say that any patisserie visited by Milcery is guaranteed success and good fortune.

title: Alcremie
text: Alcremie, the Cream Pokémon (Fairy type). When it trusts a Trainer, it will treat them to berries it’s decorated with cream. When Alcremie is content, the cream it secretes from its hands becomes sweeter and richer.

title: Falinks
text: Falinks, the Formation Pokémon (Fighting type). Other forms: Mega Falinks (Fighting). Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass’s orders are absolute. The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.

title: Pincurchin
text: Pincurchin, the Sea Urchin Pokémon (Electric type). It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines. It stores electricity in each spine. Even if one gets broken off, it still continues to emit electricity for at least three hours.

title: Snom
text: Snom, the Worm Pokémon (Ice/Bug type). It spits out thread imbued with a frigid sort of energy and uses it to tie its body to branches, disguising itself as an icicle while it sleeps. It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.

title: Frosmoth
text: Frosmoth, the Frost Moth Pokémon (Ice/Bug type). Icy scales fall from its wings like snow as it flies over fields and mountains. The temperature of its wings is less than −290 degrees Fahrenheit. It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.

title: Stonjourner
text: Stonjourner, the Big Rock Pokémon (Rock type). It stands in grasslands, watching the sun’s descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks. Once a year, on a specific date and at a specific time, they gather out of nowhere and form up in a circle.

title: Eiscue
text: Eiscue, the Penguin Pokémon (Ice type). Other forms: Noice Eiscue (Ice). It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold. This Pokémon keeps its heat-sensitive head cool with ice. It fishes for its food, dangling its single hair into the sea to lure in prey.

title: Indeedee
text: Indeedee, the Emotion Pokémon (Psychic/Normal type). Other forms: Female Indeedee (Psychic/Normal). It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need. Through its horns, it can pick up on the emotions of creatures around it. Positive emotions are the source of its strength.

title: Morpeko
text: Morpeko, the Two-Sided Pokémon (Electric/Dark type). As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It’s also generating electricity. It carries electrically roasted seeds with it as if they’re precious treasures. No matter how much it eats, it always gets hungry again in short order.

title: Cufant
text: Cufant, the Copperderm Pokémon (Steel type). It digs up the ground with its trunk. It’s also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all. If a job requires serious strength, this Pokémon will excel at it. Its copper body tarnishes in the rain, turning a vibrant green color.

title: Copperajah
text: Copperajah, the Copperderm Pokémon (Steel type). They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water. These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.

title: Dracozolt
text: Dracozolt, the Fossil Pokémon (Electric/Dragon type). In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources. The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.

title: Arctozolt
text: Arctozolt, the Fossil Pokémon (Electric/Ice type). The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around. This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.

title: Dracovish
text: Dracovish, the Fossil Pokémon (Water/Dragon type). Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction. Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can’t breathe unless it’s underwater.

title: Arctovish
text: Arctovish, the Fossil Pokémon (Water/Ice type). Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head. The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.

title: Duraludon
text: Duraludon, the Alloy Pokémon (Steel/Dragon type). Its body resembles polished metal, and it’s both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily. The special metal that composes its body is very light, so this Pokémon has considerable agility. It lives in caves because it dislikes the rain.

title: Dreepy
text: Dreepy, the Lingering Pokémon (Dragon/Ghost type). After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas. If this weak Pokémon is by itself, a mere child could defeat it. But if Dreepy has friends to help it train, it can evolve and become much stronger.

title: Drakloak
text: Drakloak, the Caretaker Pokémon (Dragon/Ghost type). It’s capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve. Without a Dreepy to place on its head and care for, it gets so uneasy it’ll try to substitute any Pokémon it finds for the missing Dreepy.

title: Dragapult
text: Dragapult, the Stealth Pokémon (Dragon/Ghost type). When it isn’t battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles. Apparently the Dreepy inside Dragapult’s horns eagerly look forward to being launched out at Mach speeds.

title: Zacian
text: Zacian, the Warrior Pokémon (Fairy type). Other forms: Crowned Zacian (Fairy/Steel). Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle. This Pokémon has slumbered for many years. Some say it’s Zamazenta’s elder sister—others say the two Pokémon are rivals.

title: Zamazenta
text: Zamazenta, the Warrior Pokémon (Fighting type). Other forms: Crowned Zamazenta (Fighting/Steel). In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle. This Pokémon slept for aeons while in the form of a statue. It was asleep for so long, people forgot that it ever existed.

title: Eternatus
text: Eternatus, the Gigantic Pokémon (Poison/Dragon type). Other forms: Eternamax Eternatus (Poison/Dragon). The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active. It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.

title: Kubfu
text: Kubfu, the Wushu Pokémon (Fighting type). Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves. If Kubfu pulls the long white hair on its head, its fighting spirit heightens and power wells up from the depths of its belly.

title: Urshifu
text: Urshifu, the Wushu Pokémon (Fighting/Dark type). Other forms: Rapid Strike Urshifu (Fighting/Water). This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist. Inhabiting the mountains of a distant region, this Pokémon races across sheer cliffs, training its legs and refining its moves.

title: Zarude
text: Zarude, the Rogue Monkey Pokémon (Dark/Grass type). Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it. Once the vines on Zarude’s body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.

title: Regieleki
text: Regieleki, the Electron Pokémon (Electric type). This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power. Its entire body is made up of a single organ that generates electrical energy. Regieleki is capable of creating all Galar’s electricity.

title: Regidrago
text: Regidrago, the Dragon Orb Pokémon (Dragon type). An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven. Its body is composed of crystallized dragon energy. Regidrago is said to have the powers of every dragon Pokémon.

title: Glastrier
text: Glastrier, the Wild Horse Pokémon (Ice type). Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force. Glastrier has tremendous physical strength, and the mask of ice covering its face is 100 times harder than diamond.

title: Spectrier
text: Spectrier, the Swift Horse Pokémon (Ghost type). It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body. As it dashes through the night, Spectrier absorbs the life-force of sleeping creatures. It craves silence and solitude.

title: Calyrex
text: Calyrex, the King Pokémon (Psychic/Grass type). Other forms: Ice Calyrex (Psychic/Ice), Shadow Calyrex (Psychic/Ghost). Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore. Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.

title: Wyrdeer
text: Wyrdeer, the Big Horn Pokémon (Normal/Psychic type). The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

title: Kleavor
text: Kleavor, the Axe Pokémon (Bug/Rock type). A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

title: Ursaluna
text: Ursaluna, the Peat Pokémon (Ground/Normal type). Other forms: Bloodmoon Ursaluna (Ground/Normal). I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.

title: Basculegion
text: Basculegion, the Big Fish Pokémon (Water/Ghost type). Other forms: Female Basculegion (Water/Ghost). Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

title: Sneasler
text: Sneasler, the Free Climb Pokémon (Fighting/Poison type). Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

title: Overqwil
text: Overqwil, the Pin Cluster Pokémon (Dark/Poison type). Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname ”sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

title: Enamorus
text: Enamorus, the Love-Hate Pokémon (Fairy/Flying type). Other forms: Therian Enamorus (Fairy/Flying). When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

title: Sprigatito
text: Sprigatito, the Grass Cat Pokémon (Grass type). The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun. Its fluffy fur is similar in composition to plants. This Pokémon frequently washes its face to keep it from drying out.

title: Floragato
text: Floragato, the Grass Cat Pokémon (Grass type). The hardness of Floragato’s fur depends on the Pokémon’s mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp. Floragato deftly wields the vine hidden beneath its long fur, slamming the hard flower bud against its opponents.

title: Meowscarada
text: Meowscarada, the Magician Pokémon (Grass/Dark type). With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on. This Pokémon uses the reflective fur lining its cape to camouflage the stem of its flower, creating the illusion that the flower is floating.

title: Fuecoco
text: Fuecoco, the Fire Croc Pokémon (Fire type). Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco’s head and flickers to and fro. It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.

title: Crocalor
text: Crocalor, the Fire Croc Pokémon (Fire type). The valve in Crocalor’s flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way. The combination of Crocalor’s fire energy and overflowing vitality has caused an egg-shaped fireball to appear on the Pokémon’s head.

title: Skeledirge
text: Skeledirge, the Singer Pokémon (Fire/Ghost type). Skeledirge’s gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. The fiery bird changes shape when Skeledirge sings. Rumor has it that the bird was born when the fireball on Skeledirge’s head gained a soul.

title: Quaxly
text: Quaxly, the Duckling Pokémon (Water type). Its strong legs let it easily swim around in even fast-flowing rivers. It likes to keep things tidy and is prone to overthinking things. This Pokémon migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago. The gel secreted by its feathers repels water and grime.

title: Quaxwell
text: Quaxwell, the Practicing Pokémon (Water type). The hardworking Quaxwell observes people and Pokémon from various regions and incorporates their movements into its own dance routines. These Pokémon constantly run through shallow waters to train their legs, then compete with each other to see which of them kicks most gracefully.

title: Quaquaval
text: Quaquaval, the Dancer Pokémon (Water/Fighting type). Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes. A single kick from a Quaquaval can send a truck rolling. This Pokémon uses its powerful legs to perform striking dances from far-off lands.

title: Lechonk
text: Lechonk, the Hog Pokémon (Normal type). This Pokémon spurns all but the finest of foods. Its body gives off an herblike scent that bug Pokémon detest. It searches for food all day. It possesses a keen sense of smell but doesn’t use it for anything other than foraging.

title: Oinkologne
text: Oinkologne, the Hog Pokémon (Normal type). Other forms: Female Oinkologne (Normal). It entrances female Pokémon with the sweet, alluring scent that wafts from all over its body. Oinkologne is proud of its fine, glossy skin. It emits a concentrated scent from the tip of its tail.

title: Tarountula
text: Tarountula, the String Ball Pokémon (Bug type). The thread it secretes from its rear is as strong as wire. The secret behind the thread’s strength is the topic of ongoing research. The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon’s natural enemy.

title: Spidops
text: Spidops, the Trap Pokémon (Bug type). Spidops covers its territory in tough, sticky threads to set up traps for intruders. It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.

title: Nymble
text: Nymble, the Grasshopper Pokémon (Bug type). It’s highly skilled at a fighting style in which it uses its jumping capabilities to dodge incoming attacks while also dealing damage to opponents. It has its third set of legs folded up. When it’s in a tough spot, this Pokémon jumps over 30 feet using the strength of its legs.

title: Lokix
text: Lokix, the Grasshopper Pokémon (Bug/Dark type). It uses its normally folded third set of legs when in Showdown Mode. This places a huge burden on its body, so it can’t stay in this mode for long. When it decides to fight all out, it stands on its previously folded legs to enter Showdown Mode. It neutralizes its enemies in short order.

title: Pawmi
text: Pawmi, the Mouse Pokémon (Electric type). The pads of its paws are electricity-discharging organs. Pawmi fires electricity from its forepaws while standing unsteadily on its hind legs. It has underdeveloped electric sacs on its cheeks. These sacs can produce electricity only if Pawmi rubs them furiously with the pads on its forepaws.

title: Pawmo
text: Pawmo, the Mouse Pokémon (Electric/Fighting type). Pawmo uses a unique fighting technique in which it uses its forepaws to strike foes and zap them with electricity from its paw pads simultaneously. When its group is attacked, Pawmo is the first to leap into battle, defeating enemies with a fighting technique that utilizes electric shocks.

title: Pawmot
text: Pawmot, the Hands-On Pokémon (Electric/Fighting type). Pawmot’s fluffy fur acts as a battery. It can store the same amount of electricity as an electric car. This Pokémon normally is slow to react, but once it enters battle, it will strike down its enemies with lightning-fast movements.

title: Tandemaus
text: Tandemaus, the Couple Pokémon (Normal type). The pair sticks together no matter what. They split any food they find exactly in half and then eat it together. Exhibiting great teamwork, they use their incisors to cut pieces out of any material that might be useful for a nest, then make off with them.

title: Maushold
text: Maushold, the Family Pokémon (Normal type). The larger pair protects the little ones during battles. When facing strong opponents, the whole group will join the fight. The two little ones just appeared one day. The group might be a family of related Pokémon, but nobody knows for sure.

title: Fidough
text: Fidough, the Puppy Pokémon (Fairy type). The yeast in Fidough’s breath is useful for cooking, so this Pokémon has been protected by people since long ago. This Pokémon is smooth and moist to the touch. Yeast in Fidough’s breath induces fermentation in the Pokémon’s vicinity.

title: Dachsbun
text: Dachsbun, the Dog Pokémon (Fairy type). The surface of this Pokémon’s skin hardens when exposed to intense heat, and its body has an appetizing aroma. The pleasant aroma that emanates from this Pokémon’s body helps wheat grow, so Dachsbun has been treasured by farming villages.

title: Smoliv
text: Smoliv, the Olive Pokémon (Grass/Normal type). This Pokémon converts nutrients into oil, which it stores in the fruit on its head. It can easily go a whole week without eating or drinking. It protects itself from enemies by emitting oil from the fruit on its head. This oil is bitter and astringent enough to make someone flinch.

title: Dolliv
text: Dolliv, the Olive Pokémon (Grass/Normal type). It basks in the sun to its heart’s content until the fruits on its head ripen. After that, Dolliv departs from human settlements and goes on a journey. Dolliv shares its tasty, fresh-scented oil with others. This species has coexisted with humans since times long gone.

title: Arboliva
text: Arboliva, the Olive Pokémon (Grass/Normal type). This Pokémon drives back enemies by launching its rich, aromatic oil at them with enough force to smash a boulder. This calm Pokémon is very compassionate. It will share its delicious, nutrient-rich oil with weakened Pokémon.

title: Squawkabilly
text: Squawkabilly, the Parrot Pokémon (Normal/Flying type). Other forms: Yellow Plumage Squawkabilly (Normal/Flying). Green-feathered flocks hold the most sway. When they’re out searching for food in the mornings and evenings, it gets very noisy. These Pokémon prefer to live in cities. They form flocks based on the color of their feathers, and they fight over territory.

title: Nacli
text: Nacli, the Rock Salt Pokémon (Rock type). The ground scrapes its body as it travels, causing it to leave salt behind. Salt is constantly being created and replenished inside Nacli’s body. It was born in a layer of rock salt deep under the earth. This species was particularly treasured in the old days, as they would share precious salt.

title: Naclstack
text: Naclstack, the Rock Salt Pokémon (Rock type). It compresses rock salt inside its body and shoots out hardened salt pellets with enough force to perforate an iron sheet. This Pokémon dry cures its prey by spraying salt over them. The curing process steals away the water in the prey’s body.

title: Garganacl
text: Garganacl, the Rock Salt Pokémon (Rock type). Many Pokémon gather around Garganacl, hoping to lick at its mineral-rich salt. Garganacl will rub its fingertips together and sprinkle injured Pokémon with salt. Even severe wounds will promptly heal afterward.

title: Charcadet
text: Charcadet, the Fire Child Pokémon (Fire type). Its firepower increases when it fights, reaching over 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. It likes berries that are rich in fat. Burnt charcoal came to life and became a Pokémon. Possessing a fiery fighting spirit, Charcadet will battle even tough opponents.

title: Armarouge
text: Armarouge, the Fire Warrior Pokémon (Fire/Psychic type). This Pokémon clads itself in armor that has been fortified by psychic and fire energy, and it shoots blazing fireballs. Armarouge evolved through the use of a set of armor that belonged to a distinguished warrior. This Pokémon is incredibly loyal.

title: Ceruledge
text: Ceruledge, the Fire Blades Pokémon (Fire/Ghost type). An old set of armor steeped in grudges caused this Pokémon’s evolution. Ceruledge cuts its enemies to pieces without mercy. The fiery blades on its arms burn fiercely with the lingering resentment of a sword wielder who fell before accomplishing their goal.

title: Tadbulb
text: Tadbulb, the EleTadpole Pokémon (Electric type). It floats using the electricity stored in its body. When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will float higher off the ground. Tadbulb shakes its tail to generate electricity. If it senses danger, it will make its head blink on and off to alert its allies.

title: Bellibolt
text: Bellibolt, the EleFrog Pokémon (Electric type). What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt’s belly-button dynamo. When this Pokémon expands and contracts its wobbly body, the belly-button dynamo in its stomach produces a huge amount of electricity.

title: Wattrel
text: Wattrel, the Storm Petrel Pokémon (Electric/Flying type). These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they’re a popular delicacy. When its wings catch the wind, the bones within produce electricity. This Pokémon dives into the ocean, catching prey by electrocuting them.

title: Kilowattrel
text: Kilowattrel, the Frigatebird Pokémon (Electric/Flying type). It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There’s hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer. Kilowattrel inflates its throat sac to amplify its electricity. By riding the wind, this Pokémon can fly over 430 miles in a day.

title: Maschiff
text: Maschiff, the Rascal Pokémon (Dark type). Its well-developed jaw and fangs are strong enough to crunch through boulders, and its thick fat makes for an excellent defense. It always scowls in an attempt to make opponents take it seriously, but even crying children will burst into laughter when they see Maschiff’s face.

title: Mabosstiff
text: Mabosstiff, the Boss Pokémon (Dark type). Mabosstiff loves playing with children. Though usually gentle, it takes on an intimidating look when protecting its family. This Pokémon can store energy in its large dewlap. Mabosstiff unleashes this energy all at once to blow away enemies.

title: Shroodle
text: Shroodle, the Toxic Mouse Pokémon (Poison/Normal type). To keep enemies away from its territory, it paints markings around its nest using a poisonous liquid that has an acrid odor. Though usually a mellow Pokémon, it will sink its sharp, poison-soaked front teeth into any that anger it, causing paralysis in the object of its ire.

title: Grafaiai
text: Grafaiai, the Toxic Monkey Pokémon (Poison/Normal type). Each Grafaiai paints its own individual pattern, and it will paint that same pattern over and over again throughout its life. The color of the poisonous saliva depends on what the Pokémon eats. Grafaiai covers its fingers in its saliva and draws patterns on trees in forests.

title: Bramblin
text: Bramblin, the Tumbleweed Pokémon (Grass/Ghost type). Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet. A soul unable to move on to the afterlife was blown around by the wind until it got tangled up with dried grass and became a Pokémon.

title: Brambleghast
text: Brambleghast, the Tumbleweed Pokémon (Grass/Ghost type). Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town. It will open the branches of its head to envelop its prey. Once it absorbs all the life energy it needs, it expels the prey and discards it.

title: Toedscool
text: Toedscool, the Woodear Pokémon (Ground/Grass type). Though it looks like Tentacool, Toedscool is a completely different species. Its legs may be thin, but it can run at a speed of 30 mph. Toedscool lives in muggy forests. The flaps that fall from its body are chewy and very delicious.

title: Toedscruel
text: Toedscruel, the Woodear Pokémon (Ground/Grass type). It coils its 10 tentacles around prey and sucks out their nutrients, causing the prey pain. The folds along the rim of its head are a popular delicacy. These Pokémon gather into groups and form colonies deep within forests. They absolutely hate it when strangers approach.

title: Klawf
text: Klawf, the Ambush Pokémon (Rock type). This Pokémon lives on sheer cliffs. It sidesteps opponents’ attacks, then lunges for their weak spots with its claws. Klawf hangs upside-down from cliffs, waiting for prey. But Klawf can’t remain in this position for long because its blood rushes to its head.

title: Capsakid
text: Capsakid, the Spicy Pepper Pokémon (Grass type). Traditional Paldean dishes can be extremely spicy because they include the shed front teeth of Capsakid among their ingredients. The more sunlight this Pokémon bathes in, the more spicy chemicals are produced by its body, and thus the spicier its moves become.

title: Scovillain
text: Scovillain, the Spicy Pepper Pokémon (Grass/Fire type). Other forms: Mega Scovillain (Grass/Fire). The green head has turned vicious due to the spicy chemicals stimulating its brain. Once it goes on a rampage, there is no stopping it. The red head converts spicy chemicals into fire energy and blasts the surrounding area with a super spicy stream of flame.

title: Rellor
text: Rellor, the Rolling Pokémon (Bug type). It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve. This Pokémon creates a mud ball by mixing sand and dirt with psychic energy. It treasures its mud ball more than its own life.

title: Rabsca
text: Rabsca, the Rolling Pokémon (Bug/Psychic type). An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably. The body that supports the ball barely moves. Therefore, it is thought that the true body of this Pokémon is actually inside the ball.

title: Flittle
text: Flittle, the Frill Pokémon (Psychic type). It spends its time running around wastelands. If anyone steals its beloved berries, it will chase them down and exact its revenge. Flittle’s toes levitate about half an inch above the ground because of the psychic power emitted from the frills on the Pokémon’s belly.

title: Espathra
text: Espathra, the Ostrich Pokémon (Psychic type). It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph. It immobilizes opponents by bathing them in psychic power from its large eyes. Despite its appearance, it has a vicious temperament.

title: Tinkatink
text: Tinkatink, the Metalsmith Pokémon (Fairy/Steel type). This Pokémon pounds iron scraps together to make a hammer. It will remake the hammer again and again until it’s satisfied with the result. It swings its handmade hammer around to protect itself, but the hammer is often stolen by Pokémon that eat metal.

title: Tinkatuff
text: Tinkatuff, the Hammer Pokémon (Fairy/Steel type). These Pokémon make their homes in piles of scrap metal. They test the strength of each other’s hammers by smashing them together. This Pokémon will attack groups of Pawniard and Bisharp, gathering metal from them in order to create a large and sturdy hammer.

title: Tinkaton
text: Tinkaton, the Hammer Pokémon (Fairy/Steel type). The hammer tops 220 pounds, yet it gets swung around easily by Tinkaton as it steals whatever it pleases and carries its plunder back home. This intelligent Pokémon has a very daring disposition. It knocks rocks into the sky with its hammer, aiming for flying Corviknight.

title: Wiglett
text: Wiglett, the Garden Eel Pokémon (Water type). Though it looks like Diglett, Wiglett is an entirely different species. The resemblance seems to be a coincidental result of environmental adaptation. This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.

title: Wugtrio
text: Wugtrio, the Garden Eel Pokémon (Water type). A variety of fish Pokémon, Wugtrio was once considered to be a regional form of Dugtrio. It has a vicious temperament, contrary to what its appearance may suggest. It wraps its long bodies around prey, then drags the prey into its den.

title: Bombirdier
text: Bombirdier, the Item Drop Pokémon (Flying/Dark type). Bombirdier uses the apron on its chest to bundle up food, which it carries back to its nest. It enjoys dropping things that make loud noises. It gathers things up in an apron made from shed feathers added to the Pokémon’s chest feathers, then drops those things from high places for fun.

title: Finizen
text: Finizen, the Dolphin Pokémon (Water type). Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole. It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.

title: Palafin
text: Palafin, the Dolphin Pokémon (Water type). Other forms: Hero Form Palafin (Water). Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen’s, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up. This Pokémon changes its appearance if it hears its allies calling for help. Palafin will never show anybody its moment of transformation.

title: Varoom
text: Varoom, the Single-Cyl Pokémon (Steel/Poison type). The steel section is Varoom’s actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities. It is said that this Pokémon was born when an unknown poison Pokémon entered and inspirited an engine left at a scrap-processing factory.

title: Revavroom
text: Revavroom, the Multi-Cyl Pokémon (Steel/Poison type). Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids. It creates a gas out of poison and minerals from rocks. It then detonates the gas in its cylinders—now numbering eight—to generate energy.

title: Cyclizar
text: Cyclizar, the Mount Pokémon (Dragon/Normal type). It can sprint at over 70 mph while carrying a human. The rider’s body heat warms Cyclizar’s back and lifts the Pokémon’s spirit. Apparently Cyclizar has been allowing people to ride on its back since ancient times. Depictions of this have been found in 10,000-year-old murals.

title: Orthworm
text: Orthworm, the Earthworm Pokémon (Steel type). This Pokémon lives in arid deserts. It maintains its metal body by consuming iron from the soil. When attacked, this Pokémon will wield the tendrils on its body like fists and pelt the opponent with a storm of punches.

title: Glimmet
text: Glimmet, the Ore Pokémon (Rock/Poison type). Glimmet’s toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself. It absorbs nutrients from cave walls. The petals it wears are made of crystallized poison.

title: Glimmora
text: Glimmora, the Ore Pokémon (Rock/Poison type). Other forms: Mega Glimmora (Rock/Poison). Glimmora’s petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels. When this Pokémon detects danger, it will open up its crystalline petals and fire beams from its conical body.

title: Greavard
text: Greavard, the Ghost Dog Pokémon (Ghost type). This friendly Pokémon doesn’t like being alone. Pay it even the slightest bit of attention, and it will follow you forever. It is said that a dog Pokémon that died in the wild without ever interacting with a human was reborn as this Pokémon.

title: Houndstone
text: Houndstone, the Ghost Dog Pokémon (Ghost type). A lovingly mourned Pokémon was reborn as Houndstone. It doesn’t like anyone touching the protuberance atop its head. Houndstone spends most of its time sleeping in graveyards. Among all the dog Pokémon, this one is most loyal to its master.

title: Flamigo
text: Flamigo, the Synchronize Pokémon (Flying/Fighting type). Thanks to a behavior of theirs known as “synchronizing,” an entire flock of these Pokémon can attack simultaneously in perfect harmony. This Pokémon apparently ties the base of its neck into a knot so that energy stored in its belly does not escape from its beak.

title: Cetoddle
text: Cetoddle, the Terra Whale Pokémon (Ice type). It lives in frigid regions in pods of five or so individuals. It loves the minerals found in snow and ice. This species left the ocean and began living on land a very long time ago. It seems to be closely related to Wailmer.

title: Cetitan
text: Cetitan, the Terra Whale Pokémon (Ice type). Ice energy builds up in the horn on its upper jaw, causing the horn to reach cryogenic temperatures that freeze its surroundings. This Pokémon wanders around snowy, icy areas. It protects its body with powerful muscles and a thick layer of fat under its skin.

title: Veluza
text: Veluza, the Jettison Pokémon (Water/Psychic type). Veluza has excellent regenerative capabilities. It sheds spare flesh from its body to boost its agility, then charges at its prey. When Veluza discards unnecessary flesh, its mind becomes honed and its psychic power increases. The spare flesh has a mild but delicious flavor.

title: Dondozo
text: Dondozo, the Big Catfish Pokémon (Water type). It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart. This Pokémon is a glutton, but it’s bad at getting food. It teams up with a Tatsugiri to catch prey.

title: Tatsugiri
text: Tatsugiri, the Mimicry Pokémon (Dragon/Water type). Other forms: Mega Curly Tatsugiri (Dragon/Water). Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack. This is a small dragon Pokémon. It lives inside the mouth of Dondozo to protect itself from enemies on the outside.

title: Annihilape
text: Annihilape, the Rage Monkey Pokémon (Fighting/Ghost type). It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core. When its anger rose beyond a critical point, this Pokémon gained power that is unfettered by the limits of its physical body.

title: Clodsire
text: Clodsire, the Spiny Fish Pokémon (Poison/Ground type). It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other. When attacked, this Pokémon will retaliate by sticking thick spines out from its body. It’s a risky move that puts everything on the line.

title: Farigiraf
text: Farigiraf, the Long Neck Pokémon (Normal/Psychic type). The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies. Now that the brain waves from the head and tail are synced up, the psychic power of this Pokémon is 10 times stronger than Girafarig’s.

title: Dudunsparce
text: Dudunsparce, the Land Snake Pokémon (Normal type). It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast. This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.

title: Kingambit
text: Kingambit, the Big Blade Pokémon (Dark/Steel type). Though it commands a massive army in battle, it’s not skilled at devising complex strategies. It just uses brute strength to keep pushing. Only a Bisharp that stands above all others in its vast army can evolve into Kingambit.

title: Great Tusk
text: Great Tusk, the Paradox Pokémon (Ground/Fighting type). This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times. Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

title: Scream Tail
text: Scream Tail, the Paradox Pokémon (Fairy/Psychic type). It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago. There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.

title: Brute Bonnet
text: Brute Bonnet, the Paradox Pokémon (Grass/Dark type). It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom. It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.

title: Flutter Mane
text: Flutter Mane, the Paradox Pokémon (Ghost/Fairy type). It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common. This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.

title: Slither Wing
text: Slither Wing, the Paradox Pokémon (Bug/Fighting type). This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine. This mysterious Pokémon has some similarities to a creature that an old book introduced as Slither Wing.

title: Sandy Shocks
text: Sandy Shocks, the Paradox Pokémon (Electric/Ground type). It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine. No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.

title: Iron Treads
text: Iron Treads, the Paradox Pokémon (Ground/Steel type). Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal. This Pokémon closely resembles a scientific weapon that a paranormal magazine claimed was sent to this planet by aliens.

title: Iron Bundle
text: Iron Bundle, the Paradox Pokémon (Ice/Water type). It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon. Its shape is similar to a robot featured in a paranormal magazine article. The robot was said to have been created by an ancient civilization.

title: Iron Hands
text: Iron Hands, the Paradox Pokémon (Fighting/Electric type). This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal. It is very similar to a cyborg covered exclusively by a paranormal magazine. The cyborg was said to be the modified form of a certain athlete.

title: Iron Jugulis
text: Iron Jugulis, the Paradox Pokémon (Dark/Flying type). It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon. It resembles a certain Pokémon introduced in a paranormal magazine, described as the offspring of a Hydreigon that fell in love with a robot.

title: Iron Moth
text: Iron Moth, the Paradox Pokémon (Fire/Poison type). No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book. This Pokémon resembles an unknown object described in a paranormal magazine as a UFO sent to observe humanity.

title: Iron Thorns
text: Iron Thorns, the Paradox Pokémon (Rock/Electric type). Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns. It has some similarities to a Pokémon introduced in a dubious magazine as a Tyranitar from one billion years into the future.

title: Frigibax
text: Frigibax, the Ice Fin Pokémon (Dragon/Ice type). This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator. Frigibax absorbs heat through its dorsal fin and converts the heat into ice energy. The higher the temperature, the more energy Frigibax stores.

title: Arctibax
text: Arctibax, the Ice Fin Pokémon (Dragon/Ice type). It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique. Arctibax freezes the air around it, protecting its face with an ice mask and turning its dorsal fin into a blade of ice.

title: Baxcalibur
text: Baxcalibur, the Ice Dragon Pokémon (Dragon/Ice type). Other forms: Mega Baxcalibur (Dragon/Ice). It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade. This Pokémon blasts cryogenic air out from its mouth. This air can instantly freeze even liquid-hot lava.

title: Gimmighoul
text: Gimmighoul, the Coin Chest Pokémon (Ghost type). Other forms: Roaming Form Gimmighoul (Ghost). It lives inside an old treasure chest. Sometimes it gets left in shop corners since no one realizes it’s actually a Pokémon. This Pokémon was born inside a treasure chest about 1,500 years ago. It sucks the life-force out of scoundrels who try to steal the treasure.

title: Gholdengo
text: Gholdengo, the Coin Entity Pokémon (Steel/Ghost type). It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession. Its body seems to be made up of 1,000 coins. This Pokémon gets along well with others and is quick to make friends with anybody.

title: Wo-Chien
text: Wo-Chien, the Ruinous Pokémon (Dark/Grass type). It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren. The grudge of a person punished for writing the king’s evil deeds upon wooden tablets has clad itself in dead leaves to become a Pokémon.

title: Chien-Pao
text: Chien-Pao, the Ruinous Pokémon (Dark/Ice type). The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon. This Pokémon can control 100 tons of fallen snow. It plays around innocently by leaping in and out of avalanches it has caused.

title: Ting-Lu
text: Ting-Lu, the Ruinous Pokémon (Dark/Ground type). It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep. The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.

title: Chi-Yu
text: Chi-Yu, the Ruinous Pokémon (Dark/Fire type). The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon. It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.

title: Roaring Moon
text: Roaring Moon, the Paradox Pokémon (Dragon/Dark type). According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region. It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.

title: Iron Valiant
text: Iron Valiant, the Paradox Pokémon (Fairy/Fighting type). It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal. It has some similarities to a mad scientist’s invention covered in a paranormal magazine.

title: Koraidon
text: Koraidon, the Paradox Pokémon (Fighting/Dragon type). This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features. This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.

title: Miraidon
text: Miraidon, the Paradox Pokémon (Electric/Dragon type). This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning. Much remains unknown about this creature. It resembles Cyclizar, but it is far more ruthless and powerful.

title: Walking Wake
text: Walking Wake, the Paradox Pokémon (Water/Dragon type). It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune. This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.

title: Iron Leaves
text: Iron Leaves, the Paradox Pokémon (Grass/Psychic type). According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders. Many of its physical characteristics match those of a Virizion from the future that was covered in a paranormal magazine.

title: Dipplin
text: Dipplin, the Candy Apple Pokémon (Grass/Dragon type). The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out. Dipplin is two creatures in one Pokémon. Its evolution was triggered by a special apple grown only in one place.

title: Poltchageist
text: Poltchageist, the Matcha Pokémon (Grass/Ghost type). Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated. Supposedly, the regrets of a tea ceremony master who died before perfecting his craft lingered in some matcha and became a Pokémon.

title: Sinistcha
text: Sinistcha, the Matcha Pokémon (Grass/Ghost type). It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset. It pretends to be tea, trying to fool people into drinking it so it can drain their life-force. Its ruse is generally unsuccessful.

title: Okidogi
text: Okidogi, the Retainer Pokémon (Poison/Fighting type). Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck. After all its muscles were stimulated by the toxic chain around its neck, Okidogi transformed and gained a powerful physique.

title: Munkidori
text: Munkidori, the Retainer Pokémon (Poison/Psychic type). Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness. The chain is made from toxins that enhance capabilities. It stimulated Munkidori's brain and caused the Pokémon's psychic powers to bloom.

title: Fezandipiti
text: Fezandipiti, the Retainer Pokémon (Poison/Fairy type). Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon. Fezandipiti owes its beautiful looks and lovely voice to the toxic stimulants emanating from the chain wrapped around its body.

title: Ogerpon
text: Ogerpon, the Mask Pokémon (Grass type). Other forms: Wellspring Mask Ogerpon (Grass/Water), Hearthflame Mask Ogerpon (Grass/Fire), Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon (Grass/Rock). This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks. This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.

title: Archaludon
text: Archaludon, the Alloy Pokémon (Steel/Dragon type). It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it. It gathers static electricity from its surroundings. The beams it launches when down on all fours are tremendously powerful.

title: Hydrapple
text: Hydrapple, the Apple Hydra Pokémon (Grass/Dragon type). These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed. Seven syrpents live inside an apple made of syrup. The syrpent in the center is the commander.

title: Gouging Fire
text: Gouging Fire, the Paradox Pokémon (Fire/Dragon type). It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil. There are scant few reports of this creature being sighted. One short video shows it rampaging and spouting pillars of flame.

title: Raging Bolt
text: Raging Bolt, the Paradox Pokémon (Electric/Dragon type). It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor. It's said to incinerate everything around it with lightning launched from its fur. Very little is known about this creature.

title: Iron Boulder
text: Iron Boulder, the Paradox Pokémon (Rock/Psychic type). It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic. It resembles a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a Terrakion that had been modified by an evil organization.

title: Iron Crown
text: Iron Crown, the Paradox Pokémon (Steel/Psychic type). There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it. It resembles a mysterious object introduced in a paranormal magazine as a cutting-edge weapon shaped like a Cobalion.

title: Terapagos
text: Terapagos, the Tera Pokémon (Normal type). Other forms: Terastal Form Terapagos (Normal), Stellar Form Terapagos (Normal). It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct. Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.

title: Pecharunt
text: Pecharunt, the Subjugation Pokémon (Poison/Ghost type). Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon. It feeds others toxic mochi that draw out desires and capabilities. Those who eat the mochi fall under Pecharunt’s control, chained to its will.
